- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Page 77: Common Math Symbols - Mathematics uses a variety of symbols to represent different operations, relationships, and concepts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. * (plus sign) – indicates addition
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. – (minus sign) – indicates subtraction
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. × (multiplication sign) – indicates multiplication
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. ÷ (division sign) – indicates division
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. = (equals sign) – indicates equality
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. ≠ (not equal sign) – indicates inequality
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. < (less than sign) – indicates that one quantity is less than another
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. > (greater than sign) – indicates that one quantity is greater than another
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. ≤ (less than or equal to sign) – indicates that one quantity is less than or equal to another
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. ≥ (greater than or equal to sign) – indicates that one quantity is greater than or equal to another
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 11. ∑ (summation symbol) – indicates the sum of a sequence of numbers or variables
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 12. ∫ (integral symbol) – indicates integration or finding the area under a curve
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 13. √ (square root symbol) – indicates finding the square root of a number
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 14. π (pi symbol) – represents the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, approximately equal to 3.14159
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 15. θ (theta symbol) – commonly used to represent an angle in geometry
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] 16. ⊥ (perpendicular symbol) – used to indicate that two lines or segments are perpendicular to each other
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These symbols are just a few of the many used in mathematics. Understanding these symbols is essential to communicating mathematical ideas effectively, and will be useful throughout your studies in math.
